author: reek
body: The refusal half of the PHY path. A model that can only answer is not a test of the driver that handles a PHY which does not, and MDIC has two distinct ways to fail that a driver can easily fold into one: the MAC never reports the transaction ready, and the MAC reports it as an error. Its `.vmargs` holds the first, which is a PHY that is not answering at all.

author: reek
body: The read must come back as the error sentinel rather than as zero. Zero is a legitimate value for most PHY registers, so a driver that returns it on a timeout has thrown the failure away -- which is the same defect the reset verdict had at CL 12079, in a different register.

author: reek
body: The bring-up must still leave the device PRESENT. This is deliberate and it is the opposite of the reset case: a part whose PHY we cannot reach may still bring a link up on its own, so refusing the device outright would be worse than trying. What the driver must not do is claim a link it never observed, and `link` below is the reading that would catch that.
